label: bad
seen: No measurement of this game exists; none was taken. I saw no score, band or tier of it or of its parent while building and labelling it; the parent's published verdicts in labelled-set.md §9 I did not open in this task.
claim: White never loses: it has a recipe under which it never loses; Black's result is not claimed.
change: two: Black's pieces become kinds of their own, moving as White's, barred from d1 and e1 (and every pawn from the far side's d and e back squares); so Black does not castle.
aim: Nothing in ordinary play leads a king onto its keep and holds it there: players castle, walk the king when the board empties, and lose it in the open, so play should be the parent's, decisive from both seats and of ordinary length. The draw is there only for a side that knows to sit.

proof.text: Every piece type carries `region` (the only squares it may ever occupy, written for White and mirrored for Black), so a piece may not move, take, promote or drop onto a square closed to it, and therefore never attacks such a square: a king standing on a square closed to every enemy piece is never in check. Here the barred kinds are Black's (`k`, `q`, `r`, `b`, `n`, all barred from d1 and e1) and the pawn, one kind for both sides (barred from d1 and e1 for Black, d8 and e8 for White); White's king, queen, rooks, bishops and knights carry no region. So a white king on e1 or d1 is never in check, hence never checkmated, and the parent has no other way for White to lose. White's recipe: play d2-d4 and then Qd1-d2 (or Qd1-d3); never castle; once the queen has left, never move any white piece but the king onto d1 or e1; move the king only between e1 and d1. Under it the king never leaves e1 and d1. It must move only when White has no other legal move, and then the other keep square holds no white piece (the recipe keeps them off it) and no black piece (none may stand there), and no black piece attacks it, so the step is legal: White is never left without a move either. Until the queen has left d1 White has other legal moves, so the king never has to move. Black's own pieces are kinds of their own (moving as White's), so White's pieces may enter d8 and e8: Black has no keep. Black's result is not claimed. Wins are reachable: in each line of `checks` a king leaves its keep and is mated.
